predecessors.name: Kingdom of France
predecessors.text: 'Henry III was forced to flee Paris, leaving Guise as de facto ruler of France' (Day of the Barricades, May 1588)

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the League-held towns and provinces returned to Henry IV, Paris in March 1594, Mayenne in January 1596, Mercœur at Angers on 20 March 1598

rulers.name: Henri I, Duke of Guise
rulers.title: head of the League; de facto ruler of France after the Barricades

rulers.name: Charles, Duke of Mayenne
rulers.title: lieutenant général de l'État et Couronne de France

ledger.x: 1588: Mercœur takes Brittany into the League.
May 1588: the Day of the Barricades; Henry III flees Paris and the League holds it.
1589: Aix-en-Provence falls to the League's armies.
5 January 1589: Mayenne secures Dijon for the Holy Union.
4 March 1589: Mayenne installs a League provincial council at Rouen.
September 1589: Henry IV defeats Mayenne at Arques.
1590: the Spanish under Parma lift the siege of Paris, which 'prepared to fight to the death rather than accept a Calvinist king'.
14 March 1590: Henry IV wins at Ivry.
1596: the League's Aix-en-Provence is no longer League-held.
January 1596: Mayenne submits and Burgundy returns to the crown.
20 March 1598: Mercœur submits at Angers, the last of the League.
March 1598: the League ends with Mercœur's submission; the Edict of Nantes follows on 13 April 1598.

wars.name: War of the Three Henrys
wars.outcome: The war 'took place during 1585–1589'; the Barricades (May 1588) put Paris in the League's hands, the Guises were assassinated on 23-24 December 1588 and Henry III was killed at Saint-Cloud in August 1589.

wars.name: French Wars of Religion (League phase)
wars.outcome: Henry IV defeated the League at Arques (1589) and Ivry (1590), converted on 25 July 1593 and entered Paris on 22 March 1594; Mayenne submitted in January 1596, Mercœur on 20 March 1598, and the Edict of Nantes followed on 13 April 1598.
